page: UpCloud GPU-12xCPU-128GB-2xL4 is a GPU-accelerated server configured with 12 vCPUs and 128.0 GB of system memory. The processing power is driven by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor using the x86_64 architecture, featuring 12 physical cores with a single thread per core on a shared CPU allocation. The server integrates two NVIDIA L4 GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, providing a combined 48 GB of VRAM. Local storage is not included in this configuration, and virtualization is managed via the KVM hypervisor.

Performance benchmarks reveal top-tier single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and single-threaded gzip compression both ranking in the top 10%. Multi-core performance and memory bandwidth metrics generally fall within the average range, though multi-threaded bzip3 decompression registers as strong. Large-block memory read bandwidth reaches 146.11 GB/sec, while write bandwidth sits at 89.37 GB/sec. For specialized tasks, the system achieves top-tier text generation speeds of 349.81 tokens/sec during small-model LLM inference, alongside average prompt processing speeds.

From a resource density perspective, the server offers a high ratio of memory to compute, providing 10.67 GB of RAM per core. The shared CPU allocation represents a potential tradeoff for sustained multi-core workloads, though this is offset by the dedicated dual-GPU acceleration. This hardware profile is suited for GPU-accelerated workloads such as machine learning inference, data science tasks, and parallel processing applications that do not require local storage.
